strongest_objection: The map's declared type is a transformation of the priced unit that names an old unit, a new unit, and what the new unit obliges, and its two most generative items are not that: Nearest countable and Dead counter are laws about how any such unit moves, stated without an old and new unit of their own. Worse, Nearest countable's law that a unit settles on the closest thing both parties can count is contradicted by three of the map's own members, since tokens, impressions, and streaming plays are counted by one side or a fourth party and the buyer merely accepts the count; the real law, visible in the map's own ford, is that the unit settles at the nearest counter both sides will accept, whoever hosts it. Dead counter's timesheet case as written does not show the mechanism it claims: a return to hourly billing needs no old timesheets, so the road back is not what closes; what the case actually shows is the new unit going blind, because a fixed bid is priced from hours and the fixed-bid shop that stopped counting hours cannot price its own unit within a season. Both items can be made members of the type by naming their transformations and keeping the conjectural law as the obligation clause, and neither needs domesticating. Beneath that, four of the seven edge labels assert a must or a cannot where a standing counterexample exists (the telecom allowance plan meters use and keeps its breakage; a platform can pay a fixed per-play rate and eat the variance; a search company hosts the meter for its own impressions; per-year insurance reopens at will), so the fork, the dependency, and the hinge stand but the incompatibility and the one-way ford survive only as conditionals.

items.item: Nearest countable: a unit settles on the closest thing both parties can count and moves the day a new counter arrives, as almond growers rent bees per hive with a frame inspection because nobody can count pollinations, and car insurance moved from per year toward per mile once an odometer plug could be mailed to the buyer; not a proxy chosen for accuracy, since the unit moves toward the newest meter rather than the truest measure (conjectural as a general law, observed in the two cases).
items.why: Not a transformation as written but a law about all of them, and the law is falsified by the map's own members: tokens, impressions, and plays are units counted by one side only, which 'both parties can count' forbids. The two cases are real transformations (an uncountable outcome retreating to an inspectable input; a period retreating to a use once a meter can be mailed) and the law belongs in the obligation clause with its modality kept.
items.repair: Nearest countable: an outcome nobody can count retreats to the nearest thing a counter both sides accept can inspect, and advances again the day a new counter arrives, as almond growers pay per hive with a frame inspection because pollination cannot be counted, and car insurance moved from per year toward per mile once an odometer plug could be mailed to the buyer; the counter need not be either party, since tokens, impressions, and plays are counted by one side or a fourth and the other side merely accepts; not a proxy chosen for accuracy, since the unit moves toward the newest accepted meter rather than the truest measure (conjectural as a general law, observed in the two cases).

items.item: Dead counter: a unit change is reversible only while the old unit's meter is still kept, and nobody is paid to keep a meter no unit bills on, so the road back closes behind the move, as a shop that went from hourly to fixed bid and stopped its timesheets can return to hourly only by bidding blind for a season; not lock-in by contract but by the decay of a measurement, a conjectured mechanism the near probe is built to test.
items.why: The case does not show the claimed mechanism. Returning to hourly billing needs no old timesheets, so 'can return to hourly only by bidding blind' is incoherent as written. What the case does show is sharper and still the author's conjecture: the new unit is priced from the old meter's records, so killing the old meter blinds the new unit. The one-way claim also holds only for moves that abandoned a meter; per-year insurance reopens at will. Repaired to name the transformation (per hour to per fixed bid) and the obligation (keep the old meter or price blind), with modality kept and the near probe still attached.
items.repair: Dead counter: per hour becomes per fixed bid, and the new unit is priced from the old one's records for exactly as long as they are kept, since nobody is paid to keep a meter no unit bills on; a shop that dropped its timesheets when it went to fixed bids is estimating blind within a season, and cannot price a return to hourly estimates either, so the road back closes only behind a move that abandoned a meter, while per-year insurance, which needed no odometer, reopens at will; not lock-in by contract but by the decay of a measurement, a conjectured mechanism the near probe is built to test.

items.item: Hostage shelf: per copy becomes per continued access, as software, film, and music sold by subscription, so the buyer's past purchases become a stake forfeited on exit and the switching cost grows with tenure; the seller acquires the obligation to stay alive and keep serving, churn becomes visible and the marginal copy invisible, and what fights it is the buyer who wanted to own; not a lease of one thing, since what is held hostage is everything the buyer accumulated.
items.why: The case list includes film sold by subscription, which has no hostage: a video-streaming subscriber forfeits nothing on exit, so that case is Sold your forecast of yourself (margin in the light viewer), not this item. The mechanism requires a stake the buyer accumulated inside the seller's house. Narrow the cases so the item's own discriminator holds.
items.repair: Hostage shelf: per copy becomes per continued access, as software holding the buyer's files and music holding the buyer's playlists sold by subscription, so the buyer's past purchases become a stake forfeited on exit and the switching cost grows with tenure; the seller acquires the obligation to stay alive and keep serving, churn becomes visible and the marginal copy invisible, and what fights it is the buyer who wanted to own; not a lease of one thing, and not film by subscription, where nothing accumulates and the margin is only the light viewer's absence, since what is held hostage is everything the buyer accumulated.

items.item: Meter in the seller's house: the unit becomes a quantity only the seller can count, as per-seat software becomes per-token inference and the buyer pays a bill they cannot audit for a tokenizer they cannot see; the measurement burden leaves the buyer and returns as trust, the cost of verbosity becomes visible while value becomes invisible, and what fights it is a buyer who cannot forecast next month's invoice; not a hidden price, since the rate is published, but a hidden count.
items.why: 'A tokenizer they cannot see' is overstated for the major vendors, who publish tokenizers or expose a count-tokens endpoint; the count the buyer genuinely cannot make is the reasoning tokens billed as output and never returned. The mechanism (a hidden count under a published rate) is right and gets stronger with the true case.
items.repair: Meter in the seller's house: the unit becomes a quantity only the seller can count, as per-seat software becomes per-token inference and the buyer pays a bill they cannot audit for reasoning tokens they are billed for and never receive; the measurement burden leaves the buyer and returns as trust, the cost of verbosity becomes visible while value becomes invisible, and what fights it is a buyer who cannot forecast next month's invoice; not a hidden price, since the rate is published, but a hidden count.

items.item: Cubed out: the priced unit migrates to whichever of the seller's constraints binds first, as a parcel carrier bills by cubic volume once its trucks fill before they weigh, and the shipping container turned per-ton handling into per-box lifts that never see the cargo; the buyer answers by packing to the unit, and what fights it is every good whose shape the unit punishes; not a unit chosen to measure value, but the seller's bottleneck given a price.
items.why: States a general law ('migrates to whichever of the seller's constraints binds first') flat, while the map marks Nearest countable's equally general law as conjectural; and the two laws pull different ways (seller's binding constraint versus nearest accepted counter) with no word on which wins. Keep the mechanism, mark the modality, and let the tension show.
items.repair: Cubed out: the priced unit tends to migrate to whichever of the seller's constraints binds first, as a parcel carrier bills by cubic volume once its trucks fill before they weigh, and the shipping container turned per-ton handling into per-box lifts that never see the cargo; the buyer answers by packing to the unit, and what fights it is every good whose shape the unit punishes, and the migration only completes where the constraint is something the buyer can measure too, a cube but not a queue; not a unit chosen to measure value, but the seller's bottleneck given a price (a tendency observed in freight, not asserted as a law).

items.item: Sold your forecast of yourself: per use becomes per right to use, as a gym membership, a season pass, or a buffet, and the seller's margin is the gap between what the buyer expects to consume and what they do, pooled across buyers so the heavy user is carried by the absent one; the buyer's intention becomes visible and their consumption invisible, and what fights it is whoever consumes as much as they expected to; not a reservation, since nothing is held for anyone and the seller sells more rights than it could honor at once.
items.why: Tested as the left neighbor below; survives.

neighbor_test.left: Sold your forecast of yourself: per use becomes per right to use, as a gym membership, a season pass, or a buffet, and the seller's margin is the gap between what the buyer expects to consume and what they do, pooled across buyers so the heavy user is carried by the absent one; the buyer's intention becomes visible and their consumption invisible, and what fights it is whoever consumes as much as they expected to; not a reservation, since nothing is held for anyone and the seller sells more rights than it could honor at once.
neighbor_test.right: Hostage shelf: per copy becomes per continued access, as software, film, and music sold by subscription, so the buyer's past purchases become a stake forfeited on exit and the switching cost grows with tenure; the seller acquires the obligation to stay alive and keep serving, churn becomes visible and the marginal copy invisible, and what fights it is the buyer who wanted to own; not a lease of one thing, since what is held hostage is everything the buyer accumulated.
neighbor_test.separating_case: Two subscriptions at the same monthly price. A video-streaming service: the subscriber leaves and forfeits nothing, the seller's margin is in the subscriber who watches two hours a month while paying for unlimited, and a price rise loses the light viewers first. A cloud design tool holding ten years of the buyer's files: the subscriber who never opens it still pays, the margin is in the exit cost, and a price rise loses the light users last. Same flat fee, opposite churn curve under a price rise, so they separate on whether the buyer's past accrues inside the seller's house; the test exposed that Hostage shelf's own 'film' case sits on the wrong side, hence the repair.

boundary_case: Bundling: per channel becomes per bundle of channels, or per application becomes per suite. Tempting because the buyer now pays for things they did not choose and the heavy user of one channel is carried by the buyer who wanted another. Ruled out: each channel is still the thing watched, no measurement burden moves, no risk moves, and the margin comes from heterogeneity of valuation across items rather than from any new obligation, so it is a change of price on unchanged units, the same class as per hour becoming per day. Where the bundle is an all-you-can-use right it is already Sold your forecast of yourself, which is the type doing its work.

seriation.note: Endpoints are real (Assay eats the item: the unit has not left the thing; Bought the forever: the unit is the seller) and the taught adjacency Sold your forecast of yourself → Thrust by the hour genuinely teaches, since the walk puts side by side the unit that lives on unseen utilization and the unit that exists to show it. The ford (Meter in the seller's house → Nearest countable → Dead counter) is the strongest stretch and becomes stronger once Dead counter says the crossing is one-way only when it abandons a meter. Three placements are arbitrary by the axis's own terms: Losers pay the winner is priced by a third population yet sits before the buyer's risk and books; Quotient, not price is a seller-side unit parked between the buyer's books and a third party's attention, a station the axis sentence never names; and Hostage shelf, continued access to the buyer's own accumulation, sits after a third party's attention because the closing hinge wants it beside Bought the forever. The author declared an itinerary rather than a scale, and the hinge earns its place, so I do not ask for a reorder, but the seriation note should admit that the last third is ordered by the walk's hinges rather than by distance from the thing.

edges.why: The incompatibility as labeled ('the seller cannot also meter that use') has a standing counterexample: the telecom allowance plan shows the buyer every unused minute on the bill and keeps its breakage, because overage is priced as a fine and the allowance is bought as a hedge against it. And 'a gym that prints visit counts on the invoice is selling thrust by the hour' is wrong: a visible count under a flat fee is still a right to use; the unit only changes when the bill is per visit. The incompatibility survives as a conditional and the map still needs it, so relabel rather than cut.
edges.repair_label: If the seller's margin comes from the buyer's non-use, a bill that shows the count puts the forecast on trial every period, and the option survives a visible meter only where the metered alternative is priced as a penalty, as the telecom allowance plan shows every unused minute and keeps its breakage by pricing overage as a fine; where use is metered at a fair rate on the same bill, the forecast dissolves and the contract has become thrust by the hour, so the two units cannot share one contract on one use unless the meter's rate is punitive (conjectural; the telecom case is the observed exception that sets the condition).

edges.why: 'The ford can be crossed only once' fails whenever the old unit needed less measurement than the new: per-year insurance reopens the moment the odometer plug is unplugged. The one-way claim holds only for a move that abandons a meter, and stating the condition sharpens the ford rather than softening it.
edges.repair_label: If the unit moves to a newer accepted meter and the old unit needed a meter of its own, nobody is paid to keep the old one and the road back closes behind the move; where the old unit needed no meter, as per-year insurance, the road back stays open, so the ford is one-way exactly in the direction that leaves a meter behind.

edges.why: 'Neither buyer nor seller can host the meter, so it must be rented from a fourth party' is contradicted by the largest attention seller alive, a search company that counts its own clicks and is accepted, grumbling, by its advertisers. The fourth party is what the buyer demands when the seller's count is not trusted, not something the unit forces; the passage between levels is real but its condition is trust, not the unit. The closing claim (capture the accepted counter and the unit is captured) is the strange part and survives.
edges.repair_label: If the unit sold is a third party's attention, the count must live wherever the buyer will accept it: in the seller's house when the seller is large enough to be trusted, as a search company counting its own clicks, and in a fourth party's when it is not, as the ratings panel that becomes the contract's real unit; either way the accepted counter is the unit, and whoever captures the counter captures the unit.

edges.why: 'The seller's unit must become a share of that stream' is not forced: a platform can pay a fixed per-play rate and carry the variance itself, and some do under minimum guarantees. The passage between levels is real but the mechanism is where the variance between a flat inflow and a variable outflow goes; the quotient is where it lands when the platform refuses to hold it.
edges.repair_label: If the buyer's per-copy payments become one flat stream while the sellers stay many, the variance between a fixed inflow and a variable count of plays must land somewhere: on the platform, if it pays a fixed rate per play and eats the gap, or on the sellers, whose unit becomes a share of the pot; the quotient is where a buyer-side metamorphosis sends the variance when the middle refuses to hold it, and it is there that the seller's price stops being a number anyone sets.

edges.why: A real fork on the sign of the event with different instruments on each branch; the antecedent fails plainly for any positive outcome.

A genuine dependency a sequence cannot show: a reservation is on a unit that only stays right while the seller's binding constraint stays put, and the lane-by-weight case makes the repricing concrete.
The hostage flipping sides is a real conditional with a failing antecedent (a renewable stream) and it is the map's best hinge.

modality_problems: Nearest countable's 'both parties can count' is stated as the general law while three members of the same map (tokens, impressions, plays) are counted by one side only; repaired to the nearest accepted counter, modality kept.

Dead counter's illustrative case does not exhibit the mechanism the item asserts; the coherent reading (new unit priced from the old meter, going blind when it dies) is a different conjecture and is now the one stated, still marked conjectural.
Cubed out states a general migration law flat where the map marks its sibling law conjectural; marked as a tendency.

Meter in the seller's house's 'a tokenizer they cannot see' is false for vendors that publish tokenizers or count-tokens endpoints; replaced with the reasoning tokens billed and never returned, which is the count the buyer truly cannot make.

Three edge labels say 'must' or 'cannot' against standing counterexamples (telecom allowance plans, fixed per-play platform rates, a search company hosting its own attention meter); relabeled as conditionals.

Rent on the peak's demand-charge case is a charge on the buyer's realized peak, billed after the fact, not a reservation of capacity held ready; the lane and the reserved instance are true reservations. The mechanism holds, but the item mixes a peak meter with two reservations and a reader will conflate them. Left as a note rather than a repair because the two clean cases carry the item.
Losers pay the winner says the buyer carries no risk; the buyer carries the risk that no one enters or no one solves, which is a different risk, not none. Minor; left in place.
duplication: none. Nearest countable and Meter in the seller's house are adjacent to witness-architectures' Common meter and Ledger that makes the debt, but this map's subject is the unit that gets priced rather than the instrument that lets a fact leave a trace, and the ledger already names the cross-field opening. No overlap with exchange-ontologies (categories of value in non-monetary deals) or passages-between-levels (Quotient is a passage, but in the pricing register with the unit as subject).
best_unresolved_seed: The map built a grammar of who hosts the meter: a grader both sides accept (Assay), the seller alone (tokens), a fourth party (the ratings panel), and nobody (the losers' unbilled attempts). It left out the buyer alone, after the fact: tipping, pay-what-you-want, the honor bar, where the count exists but the price of the service component is set by the counted party's customer after consumption. That is the mirror of Meter in the seller's house, a meter in the buyer's house, and it would test whether the map's laws of unit motion run symmetrically: does a unit also settle on the nearest counter the seller will accept, and does a buyer-hosted meter die the same way? Behind it sits the second seed: the map now carries two attractors, the seller's binding constraint (Cubed out) and the nearest accepted counter (Nearest countable), and has no rule for which wins when they disagree.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing five items (recasting Nearest countable and Dead counter as transformations that carry their laws as conjectural obligations, since the first was contradicted by three of the map's own one-sided meters and the second's case showed a different mechanism than it claimed; narrowing Hostage shelf's cases to ones with a hostage; correcting the token-count and freight-law modalities) and relabeling four edges whose musts and cannots had standing counterexamples, so the incompatibility and the one-way ford now hold as conditionals.
